stem.en: Adjustments are made while preparing financial statements mainly to follow the:

options.en: Money measurement concept
Cash basis of accounting
Accrual and matching concepts
Business entity concept only

explanation.en: Adjustments bring in all incomes earned and expenses incurred for the period, whether received or paid or not.

stem.en: Closing stock given as an adjustment (outside the trial balance) is shown on the:

options.en: Credit side of the trading account and assets side of the balance sheet
Debit side of the trading account only
Liabilities side of the balance sheet
Credit side of the profit and loss account only

explanation.en: Closing Stock A/c Dr To Trading A/c: it is credited in the trading account and shown as a current asset.

stem.en: Every adjustment given outside the trial balance is generally shown in the financial statements:

options.en: At two places
At three places
Only in a note
At one place

explanation.en: Because of double entry, each adjustment affects two items: usually one in trading or P&L and one in the balance sheet.

stem.en: Goods costing ₹3,000 taken by the proprietor for personal use are recorded by:

options.en: Drawings A/c Dr To Sales A/c ₹3,000
Drawings A/c Dr To Purchases A/c ₹3,000
Purchases A/c Dr To Drawings A/c ₹3,000
Capital A/c Dr To Cash A/c ₹3,000

explanation.en: The goods were bought for business but taken out by the owner, so drawings increase and purchases decrease.

stem.en: Outstanding rent is shown in the balance sheet as a:

options.en: Current asset
Deduction from capital
Current liability
Fixed asset

explanation.en: Rent due but not yet paid is an amount the business owes.

stem.en: Rent shown in the trial balance is ₹22,000 for 11 months, the monthly rent being ₹2,000. The rent debited to profit and loss is:

explanation.en: One month (₹2,000) is outstanding: 22,000 + 2,000 = ₹24,000.

stem.en: An insurance premium of ₹9,600 was paid on 1 July 2024 for one year. Books are closed on 31 March 2025. The prepaid insurance is:

explanation.en: The premium covers July 2024 to June 2025; April–June 2025 (3 months) is prepaid: 9,600 × 3/12 = ₹2,400.

stem.en: The adjusting entry for wages outstanding is:

options.en: Outstanding Wages A/c Dr To Wages A/c
Wages A/c Dr To Outstanding Wages A/c
Wages A/c Dr To Cash A/c
Profit and Loss A/c Dr To Wages A/c

explanation.en: The expense is increased (Wages Dr) and a liability is created (Outstanding Wages Cr).

stem.en: The amount of salaries debited to the profit and loss account is:

explanation.en: Outstanding salary is added: 66,000 + 6,000 = ₹72,000. The ₹6,000 also appears as a current liability.

passage.en: The trial balance of Veena Traders on 31 March 2025 shows: Salaries ₹66,000; Insurance ₹8,000; Rent received ₹30,000; Sundry debtors ₹1,20,000; Bad debts ₹2,000. Adjustments: (a) salaries for March 2025, ₹6,000, are outstanding; (b) insurance prepaid ₹2,000; (c) rent received includes ₹5,000 for April 2025; (d) further bad debts ₹4,000; (e) create a provision for doubtful debts at 5% on debtors.

stem.en: Accrued income is shown in the balance sheet as a:

options.en: Deduction from capital
Current liability
Current asset
Fixed asset

explanation.en: Income earned but not yet received is an amount receivable, so it is a current asset.

stem.en: Income received in advance is:

options.en: Deducted from the income and shown as a liability
Added to capital
Ignored until the next year
Added to the income and shown as an asset

explanation.en: It belongs to the next period, so it is removed from this year's income and shown as a current liability.

stem.en: A firm holds 10% investments of ₹80,000 for the full year. Interest received during the year is ₹6,000. Accrued interest is:

explanation.en: Interest due for the year = 10% × 80,000 = 8,000; received 6,000; accrued = ₹2,000.

stem.en: Commission received shown in the trial balance is ₹15,000. It includes ₹3,000 received in advance, and ₹2,000 commission earned is yet to be received. Commission credited to profit and loss is:
The provision for doubtful debts is calculated on debtors after deducting:

options.en: Creditors
Bills payable
Further bad debts
Provision for discount

explanation.en: Debts already known to be bad are written off first; the provision is on the remaining (good) debtors.

stem.en: Debtors ₹50,000; further bad debts ₹2,000; provision for doubtful debts is to be 5%. The provision is:
Provision for discount on debtors is calculated on debtors after deducting:

options.en: Further bad debts and the new provision for doubtful debts
Only further bad debts
Only the provision for doubtful debts
Nothing

explanation.en: Discount is allowed only to good debtors who pay, so both further bad debts and doubtful debts provision are deducted first.

stem.en: Bad debts in the trial balance ₹1,500; further bad debts ₹500; old provision for doubtful debts ₹3,000; new provision 5% on debtors of ₹60,000 (before further bad debts). The net amount charged to profit and loss is:

explanation.en: Debtors after further bad debts = 59,500; new provision = 2,975. Charge = 1,500 + 500 + 2,975 − 3,000 = ₹1,975.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Provision for doubtful debts is a charge against the profit of the current year.
Reason (R): It is created for an expected loss on debtors whose exact amount cannot be known now.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true, and R explains A: an expected loss of the current year's credit sales is charged to the current year (prudence and matching).

stem.en: The provision for doubtful debts to be created is:

explanation.en: Good debtors = 1,20,000 − 4,000 (further bad debts) = 1,16,000. Provision = 5% × 1,16,000 = ₹5,800.

passage.en: The trial balance of Veena Traders on 31 March 2025 shows: Salaries ₹66,000; Insurance ₹8,000; Rent received ₹30,000; Sundry debtors ₹1,20,000; Bad debts ₹2,000. Adjustments: (a) salaries for March 2025, ₹6,000, are outstanding; (b) insurance prepaid ₹2,000; (c) rent received includes ₹5,000 for April 2025; (d) further bad debts ₹4,000; (e) create a provision for doubtful debts at 5% on debtors.

stem.en: A manager is entitled to a commission of 5% on net profit before charging the commission. Net profit before commission is ₹1,00,000. The commission is:
Net profit before charging manager's commission is ₹1,05,000. The manager gets 5% of net profit after charging such commission. The commission is:

explanation.en: Commission = 1,05,000 × 5/105 = ₹5,000. Check: profit after commission 1,00,000; 5% of it = 5,000.

stem.en: The journal entry for interest on capital is:

options.en: Cash A/c Dr To Interest on Capital A/c
Capital A/c Dr To Interest on Capital A/c
Interest on Capital A/c Dr To Capital A/c
Interest on Capital A/c Dr To Cash A/c

explanation.en: Interest on capital is an expense to the business and is credited (added) to the proprietor's capital.

stem.en: Capital on 1 April 2024 was ₹3,00,000. Additional capital of ₹60,000 was introduced on 1 October 2024. Interest on capital is 10% p.a. and books close on 31 March 2025. Interest on capital is:

Assertion (A): Interest on capital is debited to the profit and loss account.
Reason (R): Interest on capital is a gain for the business.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true. R is false: interest on capital is an expense for the business (and an income for the proprietor), which is why it is debited to profit and loss.

stem.en: Debtors ₹60,000; bad debts in the trial balance ₹1,500; further bad debts ₹1,000; old provision for doubtful debts ₹2,500; new provision at 5% on debtors. The total amount debited to the profit and loss account for bad and doubtful debts is:
Net profit before charging the manager's commission is ₹1,32,000. The manager is entitled to 10% of the net profit after charging such commission. His commission is:
Insurance premium of ₹18,000 was paid on 1 August 2024 for one year. Accounts are closed on 31 March 2025. The amount charged to the profit and loss account is:

explanation.en: August 2024 to March 2025 is 8 months: 18,000 × 8/12 = ₹12,000 to P&L; the remaining ₹6,000 (April–July 2025) is prepaid insurance, a current asset.
